unit.why: A single narrative: the Besht follows a dancing bear to the judge's house, where the bear digs up a hidden dead infant, which foils a planned blood libel.
unit.boundary_note: Contains an embedded page-header catchword ('174 גם שבחי הבעש״ט 175') from the print.

stories.start_quote: פ"א בשבת שקודם פסח התפלל הרב
stories.summary_en: On the Sabbath before Passover the Besht leaves prayers to follow a bear to the judge's house, where the bear digs up a dead infant hidden there to frame the Jews; the Besht calls the onlookers to witness and returns to finish praying.

tags.why: The tale's arc is the Besht averting a blood libel against the Jews.

tags.why: He shields the community from a libel by calling public witnesses.
